title: Reinforcement Learning Fine-Tuning for Instruction Following and Math Reasoning
abstract: This study investigates the effectiveness of reinforcement learning fine-tuning techniques on a compact language model for instruction following and mathematical reasoning tasks.

sections.title: The Core Insight
sections.content:
Imagine you're trying to teach a language model to follow instructions. You could use traditional supervised learning, but what if you could fine-tune it using reinforcement learning? This approach allows the model to learn from feedback and improve its performance over time.

In this study, we explore the application of reinforcement learning fine-tuning techniques to a small-scale language model, Qwen2.5-0.5B Base, on two distinct tasks: instruction following and math reasoning.

sections.title: How It Works
sections.content:
We compare three fine-tuning approaches: supervised fine-tuning (SFT), Direct Preference Optimization (DPO), and Reinforce Leave-One-Out (RLOO). Each approach has its strengths and weaknesses. For example, DPO uses a contrastive loss to optimize the model, while RLOO uses a leave-one-out baseline to reduce variance in the gradient estimates.

We also experiment with different reward models, including DeBERTa, DistilBERT, and Siamese DistilBERT, to guide the fine-tuning process.

sections.title: Benchmark Results
sections.content:
Our experiments show that RLOO with DeBERTa reward modeling achieves the best alignment, while DPO provides strong and consistent results. For math reasoning tasks, synthetic data augmentation and best-of-N sampling with an external verifier significantly improve accuracy.

sections.title: Why This Matters
sections.content:
The results of this study have significant implications for the development of language models that can follow instructions and reason mathematically. By using reinforcement learning fine-tuning techniques, we can improve the performance of small-scale language models, making them more suitable for deployment in resource-constrained environments.

Furthermore, the use of external verifiers and best-of-N sampling can significantly improve the accuracy of math reasoning tasks, demonstrating the potential of combining fine-tuning with inference-time tools.

sections.title: Key Innovations
sections.content:
This study contributes several key innovations, including the use of DeBERTa reward modeling in the RLOO framework and the application of best-of-N sampling with an external verifier for math reasoning tasks. These innovations demonstrate the potential of combining fine-tuning with inference-time tools to improve the performance of language models.

Furthermore, the study highlights the importance of using high-quality reward models and external verifiers to guide the fine-tuning process and improve the accuracy of math reasoning tasks.

sections.title: Try It Yourself
sections.content:
To try out the fine-tuning approaches and reward models used in this study, you can access the code repository at https://github.com/Yifu93/LLM-Reinforcement-Learning. The repository provides implementation details and instructions for reproducing the results.

You can also experiment with different fine-tuning approaches and reward models to see how they affect the performance of the language model on instruction following and math reasoning tasks.
